cognate: Arm. tam ~ Gk δίδωμι ~ Skt dadāti (*deh3-); Arm. dowstr ~ Gk θυγάτηρ ~ Skt duhitár- (*dʰugh2tḗr); reflexive possessive Arm. iwr ~ Gk ἥν / ἑαυτοῦ ~ Skt svām
drift_or_renewal: Greek prose renews the reflexive (ἑαυτοῦ for Homeric ἥν); Arm. adds predicative kin / i kənowtʻiwn 'as wife' (cf. Skt bhāryā-arthe, Hitt. ANA DAM-UTTI, recalled)
shared_syntax: father (subject) + 'give' + acc. 'daughter' + reflexive possessive + dative of the bridegroom
context: dynastic marriage notices in historiography: a ruler gives his own daughter to an ally/noble (Movses: Artašam to Mihrdat; Thucydides: Hippias' daughter Archedike to Aiantides); Homer's Lycian king gives Bellerophon his daughter (Il. 6.192); epic Sanskrit dadau duhitaraṃ tasmai is the standing expression of the kanyādāna
phrase: *dʰugh2tér-m̥ (swo-) deh3- 'give (one's own) daughter (in marriage) to X'
note: Exact cognate verb+object in the same legal-social act in Greek (Homer onward), Armenian (Faustos, Movses, Łazar repeatedly) and Sanskrit epic; reflects the IE institution of the father giving the bride (Benveniste, recalled). Low because both words are core vocabulary and the act is everywhere expressed this way where the words survive; Latin (filiam dare/nuptum dare) and Germanic (gefa dóttur) renew the verb or keep it only partly. Armenian is a 5th-c. Christian historiography, but the marriage phrasing is native narrative.

near_miss.lead: addressed/questioned person stays silent: ON Spurði ... þagðe við ~ Lat. saluete inquam ... atque illi tacent (þegja ~ taceo, *teh2k-)
near_miss.why_not: Exact cognate verb in a congruent narrative slot, but 'ask - be silent' is ordinary narrative language and the verb survives only in Germanic and Italic as the basic word for 'be silent'; nothing formulaic beyond the verb.

near_miss.lead: fé ~ pecus ~ paśu; ON fatœkra manna fe ('poor men's property') vs AVP manuṣyāḥ paśavaḥ ('men, cattle') as a reflex of the *wiHro-peḱu merism
near_miss.why_not: ON is a genitive 'men's money' in a speech about a gift of silver, not a men-and-cattle merism; Cato's pecus consideret is farm management. Shared vocabulary only.

near_miss.lead: Ir. cor bris a craide ina cliab 'broke her heart in her breast'
near_miss.why_not: No partner continues heart-in-breast wording; the Irish is a stock Acallam spear-cast; generic anatomy.

near_miss.lead: Sigurðr va ormenn 'Sigurd slew the serpent' (vega *weik- + ormr *wr̥mis) as a dragon-slaying formula; Lucretius uictae shares *weik-
near_miss.why_not: No partner has a serpent-slaying; vega/uinco in unrelated contexts. The PIE dragon-slaying formula is *gʷʰen- + *h1ógʷʰis (Ved. áhann áhim), which ON renews in both terms; not defensible as a cognate collocation.

near_miss.lead: 'bring' + abstract (pacem fero ~ vitni fram bera) and ON marger menn leto lif sitt 'many lost their lives'
near_miss.why_not: bʰer- + object is generic; pax and vitni are not cognate; láta líf has no partner. No shared phrase.

near_miss.lead: κλέος / mikils virði 'great fame of a woman' ~ ON konongr virði þa mikils
near_miss.why_not: Not cognate in the key terms (κλέος vs virða); praise of persons is generic.

near_miss.lead: figura etymologica dóm dœma 'judge a judgment' (*dʰoh1-mo-) vs Ved. dhā- with its nouns
near_miss.why_not: ON figure is internal Germanic (dœma denominal from dómr); AV ratna-dhām is a compound epithet, not a figure; no congruent context.

near_miss.lead: *kowh2-: ON hoggva 'hew' vs Russ. кована и вязана 'fettered and bound' / ORV ковати мужа
near_miss.why_not: Byliny pair кован и вязан is a Russian formula with a chronicle antecedent (same branch only); ON hœggr is 'strike with sword', different meaning and context. No cross-branch collocation.

near_miss.lead: hvítt sem snior 'white as snow' (*ḱweyt- + *snoygʷʰos; cf. Russ. бѣлъ яко снѣгъ, Lith. baltas kaip sniegas, Il. 10.437 λευκότεροι χιόνος)
near_miss.why_not: No partner in the slab has the simile; Slavic and later forms are biblical-influenced and the colour words are renewed; a natural simile, not demonstrably inherited.

near_miss.lead: heart in the breast: ON brióst ... hiarta ~ Ir. ósa broind ... a chridi 'na chlíab (hiarta ~ cride *ḱḗr; brióst ~ brú *bʰrus-)
near_miss.why_not: Two cognate body words, but ON is a king's healing touch on the breast near the heart, the Irish a spear piercing the heart; the Irish brú is the belly the shield covers, not the seat of the heart. Generic anatomy, incongruent contexts.

error.correct_reading: brú 'belly, womb' (dat. broinn) < *bʰrus- / *bʰrews- 'swell', cognate with ON brióst, OE brēost (recalled, Matasović s.v. *brusū)
error.evidence: Lemma correctly identified but left unmapped; same in mga:G301035:#1/4/#1:316.

error.correct_reading: cride 'heart' (acc. sg., a cride 'her heart'), < *ḱḗr; context 'cor bris a craide ina cliab'
error.evidence: OCR/late spelling of cride; same phrase in G301035 has chridi mapped to *ḱḗr.

error.correct_reading: co ro (conjunction co + perfective ro) before bris 'broke'
error.evidence: Syntax 'co tarla ... cor bris': consecutive conjunction, not the noun cor.

error.correct_reading: sleg 'spear' (in t-shleg, nom. sg. with article)
error.evidence: Same word lemmatized as sleg in mga:G303000:#1:1872.
